newsitem.title: UK: Quintain to buy Fiscal Properties.
newsitem.headline: Quintain to buy Fiscal Properties.

text.p: Britain's Quintain Estates and Development Plc said on Thursday it agreed to buy Fiscal Properties Plc and other interests in a recommended offer worth 77 million stg.
As part of the deal, Quintain said it would buy interests in Croydon Land and Estates Ltd not owned by Fiscal.
Quintain said it would offer 73 new Quintain shares for every 140 Fiscal shares in a bid valuing each Fiscal share at 72.7p, a premium of 12 percent to Wednesday's closing price of 65p.
The offer valued Fiscal at 60.0 million stg, the companies said in a joint statement.
Quintain said it would offer a partial cash alternative enabling Fiscal shareholders to elect to receive 71p for each Fiscal share.
The company said it would offer 76.698 new Quintain shares for every 100 stg nominal of Fiscal loan stock.
Quintain said it would pay for Croydon Land and Estates with 8.4 million stg in new Quintain shares and 8.3 million stg in cash.
The company said it planned to sell some of Fiscal's and Croydon's properties, valued at about 50 million stg, that did not fit into its investment criteria.
As a result of the deal, Quintain's pro forma gross assets would more than double to about 253 million stg with net assets of some 105 million stg, equivalent to 128p per share.
Quintain said that following the offers, Nigel Ellis, currently non-executive chairman, had agreed to become executive chairman.
"Fiscal's portfolio provides high quality secure cash flow, and the Croydon Land portfolio offers significant marriage value potential," Quintain said.
Fiscal's shares were marked up 4.5p at 69.5 by 0825 GMT, while Quintain's shares slid 1.0p to 138.5. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
